findings.text: M0's complete static observation needs MP's inputs (the seven packages, the runtime with its install receipts, the reader tree). At MI the M0 controls therefore reach the real entries static_check and observe_host only through refusals that occur before the source binding, with the observer's host boundary substituted (ControlHost, labelled mocked). MC10 additionally substitutes M0's static facts (static_observation and static_after_start), which is more than the contract's 'simulated at the command boundary'. Recommendation: MH re-runs MC10 with real static bindings and only the command boundary simulated; plan section 6 does not list MC10 for MH.

W5's interface (section 6) names the boundaries whose substitution labels a result mocked: the Darwin run_process, os.uname, the observer's readers, python_inventory, check_runtime, check_git_binding, and the provider's own host_state, _selection and _verify_host. Besides run_process, host_state and _verify_host, the provider's attempt controls also substitute _host_git, _verify_source, _cross_bindings, _verify_dependencies and _verify_methods, which are not listed, so that the provider's own configuration digest check, contract and adoption-record bindings, manifest, job checks and boot binding stay real. The records are labelled mocked through the listed substitutions, and the controls assert that label. These are private names; a rename makes the controls fail visibly, not pass.

At MI the detection of a source, runtime or dependency change after preflight is simulated at its verification boundary, since the real detectors need MP's inputs; the job-input and configuration changes are detected by the provider's own code. Recommendation: MH re-runs MC29 with the real detectors.

host_state is simulated, and the check against HOST inside _verify_host is substituted, so MI exercises the provider's comparisons before and after the start only. No MI control runs the provider's real host_state reader (kern.bootsessionuuid and both SystemVersion.plist copies); MH runs it on the qualifying host.

The driver has no rule of its own for a method that is missing without an error (W4 interface section 7; D-08). The MI case simulates the provider's cohort accounting by a class teardown error. The provider's finish_cpu_cohort calls verify_case_manifest, which needs a complete selection, so its missing-method decision is not frozen at MI; it belongs to MH together with MC28.

MC38 asserts its premise that the real SIGTERM send to a group of one exited, unreaped member is refused with EPERM, because the contract says the case 'also covers the handling of a send refused with EPERM'; MC39 (a) asserts that the owned group still answers EPERM after run_process. On a build where Darwin answers otherwise these cases fail visibly instead of passing without the stated coverage. MC37 does not require EPERM: it requires that the raw answer is not ESRCH while the child is unreaped and is ESRCH after reaping, as the amended trust assumption states.

A malformed or mismatched 0.2.0 selection reaching the facade is dispatched to the 0.1.0 code, whose refusal records are refusal/0.1.0 documents without the 0.2.0 labels (compare W5 interface Q4 for the ordinary run). The refusal and the zero starts hold, which is all the controls assert; whether such records meet contract section 10 and plan section 5 is left to the independent reviewer (W7).

The preparer stages on the destination's own volume and refuses otherwise, so a real failing renamex_np inside the flow is reachable only by redirecting the call's destination argument to another volume; the call and its EXDEV failure are real.

The probe's reviewed dynamic constructs load the bound validator, Three.js and GLTFLoader entries; the absence of process creation in those files can only be shown by the MH scan of the 24 reader files and the module loader.
